findings.claim: mHC, DSA and stable GRPO appeared without a first-use expansion or a sufficiently precise functional gloss.
findings.current_state: mHC is expanded as Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections; DSA is expanded as DeepSeek Sparse Attention; the GRPO phrase now states that the protocol stabilizes and extends GRPO-based RL.

findings.claim: The five-axis current framework named input-boundary and depth-mixing changes without giving them a foundation contract comparable to the other axes.
findings.current_state: Lines 142-151 now add an input-boundary equation and FormulaNote, then contrast the baseline previous-layer input, depth mixing, and the residual update.

findings.claim: The 6-to-2 depth mixer was hardcoded while the surrounding lab invited the reader to change architecture numbers, leaving its static status unclear.
findings.current_state: The metric and verdict now explicitly mark 6-to-2 depth mixing as a fixed property of the synthetic specification, separate from the adjustable controls.

hidden_transfer.claim: A cost reduction on one architecture axis may move pressure to another axis instead of eliminating it.
hidden_transfer.evidence: The paper protocol asks the cost-shift question and the lab verdict now explicitly distinguishes independently adjustable memory and active-capacity axes from fixed input/depth properties.

accepted_reviews.source_boundary: The Claude pass did not independently browse 2026 current sources; the article itself labels the five-axis framework as an editorial reconstruction and separates vendor claims from independent evaluation.

findings.current_state: Lines 141-147 now state non-commutativity, use A_t A_(t-1) ... A_(i+1), explain application order, and define the empty product at i=t.
